translations.text: This is the Wish of Manchán of Liath:
I wish, O Son of the living God, O eternal, ancient King, for a hidden little hut in the wilderness, so that it may be my dwelling,
A clear grey-green, shallow stream to be beside it, a clear pool to wash away sins through the grace of the Holy Spirit,
A beautiful wood close by, around it on every side, for the nurture of many-voiced birds, as a shelter to hide it,
Facing south for warmth, a little brook across its ground, choice land of great abundance that would be good for every plant,
A few sensible young men (we shall make known their number), humble and obedient, to pray to the King:
Four threes, three fours (fit for every need), two sixes in the church, both north and south;
Six pairs besides myself, praying through the long ages to the King who makes the sun shine;
A pleasant church with linen cloth, a dwelling for God from heaven; and then bright candles above the pure, white Scripture,
One house to go to for the care of the body, without wantonness [?], without self-indulgence [?], without thinking of evil.
This is the husbandry I would take up; I would choose it openly: fresh, fragrant leeks, hens, speckled salmon, bees,—
My fill of clothing and food from the King of fair fame, and for me to be sitting there for a while, praying to God in every place.
